requirements.requirement: Identify the unexpected space consumer on /srv/archive.
requirements.summary: Direct inspection isolated the hidden telemetry cache and its single 690,073,600-byte collector-debug.capture file; no process held it open.
Utilization was directly measured at 100% before removal and 7% afterward, with approximately 690 MB available.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the existing archiveapp identity can write to /srv/archive/incoming.
requirements.summary: The initial archiveapp write failed with ENOSPC. After recovery, archiveapp successfully created and synced a 17-byte file with archiveapp:archiveapp ownership and mode 0640; the probe was then removed.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the archive filesystem and its existing archive data.
requirements.summary: The filesystem remained mounted read-write as XFS on /dev/loop0. The prepared manifest checksum, ownership, permissions, and size remained unchanged after recovery, while only the identified unexpected capture was removed.

requirements.requirement: Perform the recovery without taking the server offline.
requirements.summary: The archive mount was available before and after the repair, and lifecycle observations retained the same boot-scoped identifier, listening sockets, and process IDs. This coherently supports an online recovery without reboot or unmount.

overall_summary: All material outcomes were satisfied: the unexpected debug capture was identified and removed, utilization fell from 100% to 7%, archiveapp write behavior recovered, and the XFS filesystem and known archive records remained intact during an online repair.
limitations: No explicit post-execution boot_id or continuous external availability probe was captured; online continuity is supported by unchanged process IDs, sockets, boot-scoped paths, and mount state.
Archive-data preservation was verified against the prepared records inventory and manifest, rather than through a whole-filesystem pre/post content hash.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-space-consumer
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: archive-filesystem-identity, archive-manifest-hash, archive-manifest-metadata
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: executor-start-boot-id

operational_hygiene.summary: No unwanted executor residue or system degradation is evident. Both write probes were removed, no services failed, listening sockets remained unchanged, and package health remained clean. The systemd-hostnamed private-directory suffix change is normal transient lifecycle churn.
